question:
(a) State Ohm's law and mention the condition for its validity.
(b) Explain why Ohm's law is not a universal law.
(c) A device has $V-I$ readings: $(1\,\text{V},0.2\,\text{A})$, $(2\,\text{V},0.5\,\text{A})$ and $(3\,\text{V},1.0\,\text{A})$. Check whether it obeys Ohm's law.

options.A:
(a) Ohm's law states $V\propto 1/I$ at constant temperature.
(b) It is universal for all devices.
(c) $V/I=5\,\Omega,4\,\Omega,3\,\Omega$; therefore the device obeys Ohm's law.
options.B:
(a) Ohm's law states $V=I/R$.
(b) It fails only when voltage is zero.
(c) The device obeys Ohm's law because current increases with voltage.
options.C:
(a) Ohm's law states that current is independent of voltage.
(b) It is not universal because resistance is always zero.
(c) The device has constant resistance $5\,\Omega$.
options.D:
(a) Ohm's law states $V=IR$ or $I\propto V$, provided physical conditions such as temperature remain constant.
(b) It is not universal because many devices have a non-linear $V-I$ relation and non-constant $V/I$.
(c) $V/I=5\,\Omega,4\,\Omega,3\,\Omega$, so the device does not obey Ohm's law.
